inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.constructor.host
inputs.description: The remote host this service acts on, passed in as the RemoteHostService itself: `current()` yields the enabled record and the running runtime, `saved()` writes the record, `published()` announces the status, and `name()` names this computer. `current()` throws 'Turn remote access on first.' while remote access is off, so every operation rejects then.

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.constructor.registry
inputs.description: The project registry, used only through `list()` by `approvePairing`: each project named in an approval must be among the registered projects, and its `id` and `name` are copied into the grant. A rejection from `list()` makes the approval reject too.

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.approvePairing.input
inputs.description: The approval the person made, validated by `RemoteInputValidator.approval`: exactly the keys `agents`, `deviceId`, `pairingId` and `projectIds`, plus an optional boolean `comments` that must be `true` when `agents` is `true` and `comments` is given. `projectIds` takes 1 to 64 distinct `local-` project ids, `pairingId` 32 and `deviceId` 40 lowercase hex characters, and any other shape is refused with 'The request was not understood.'

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.denyPairing.input
inputs.description: The pairing request to refuse, validated by `RemoteInputValidator.pairing`: an object with exactly the key `pairingId`, which is 32 lowercase hex characters naming the open offer. A value that matches no waiting request changes nothing, and the current status is still returned.

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.revokeDevice.input
inputs.description: The phone to revoke, validated by `RemoteInputValidator.device`: an object with exactly the key `deviceId`, which is 40 lowercase hex characters. The id joins the revoked list whether or not it is an approved device, and the relay is told at once or as soon as it can be reached.

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.dropped.deviceId
inputs.description: The id of a phone the owner revoked through the hub, used as given with no format check. The approved device with this id is removed and its session ended, and the record is saved even when no device matches.

inputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.seen.deviceId
inputs.description: The id of a phone whose relay connection has just closed, used as given with no format check. Only an approved device with this id gets `lastSeenAt` set to the current time and a saved record; any other id returns without saving.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.createPairing
outputs.description: The one-time offer shown as a QR code: its `pairingId`, `hostId`, `origin`, the typed `code` as `XXXX-XXXX`, the exact QR text in `scan`, and `expiresAt`, five minutes after it was opened. It resolves only once the relay has accepted the offer and the host has published it, and opening it replaces any earlier offer.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.closePairing
outputs.description: The host status once the open offer has been withdrawn, so `pairing` and `requests` are empty. The relay is told to close the offer when one was open, and an unreachable relay does not make this call fail.

examples.reason: The relay cannot be reached. Paired phones are offline.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.approvePairing
outputs.description: The host status after the phone was approved: it is listed in `devices` with the granted projects, agents and comments, and the offer and its request are gone. It resolves once the relay has accepted the approval; if the relay refuses it or cannot be reached, the devices are restored and the call rejects.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.denyPairing
outputs.description: The host status after the waiting request was refused, which closes the offer and tells the relay, so `pairing` and `requests` are empty. A `pairingId` with no waiting request changes nothing, and the status is returned as it is.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.revokeDevice
outputs.description: The host status after the phone was removed from `devices` and its session ended, returned once the record is saved. Each revoked id is sent to the relay during the call; an id the relay could not be reached about stays in the revoked list and is sent again when the relay is back.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.dropped
outputs.description: Resolves with nothing once the phone has been removed from the approved devices, its session has ended, and the record is saved. The owner revoked it through the hub, so the relay already knows and nothing is sent to it.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.seen
outputs.description: Resolves with nothing; an approved device with this id gets `lastSeenAt` set to the current time and the record is saved, while any other id resolves without saving anything. It is called when that phone's relay connection closes.

outputs.name: RemotePairingControlService.flush
outputs.description: Resolves with nothing after each id in the revoked list has been sent to the relay: an id the relay answered leaves the list, and one it could not be reached about stays there. This call does not save the record.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by the host's `current()` with the message 'Turn remote access on first.' whenever remote access is off. Every operation calls `current()`, so every operation can reject with it.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by `createPairing` before any offer is opened, with the message 'The relay of this computer cannot be shown to a phone as a QR code.', when the computer's relay origin is missing or is not one an offer may carry.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Rejected by the relay command with the message 'The relay is not connected.' when the relay socket is not online or drops while a command waits; `createPairing` and `approvePairing` pass it on unchanged.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Rejected by the relay command with the message 'The relay did not answer.' when no acknowledgement arrives within the ack timeout, 10 seconds by default; `createPairing` and `approvePairing` pass it on unchanged.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Rejected by the relay command when the relay acknowledges a command with ok set to false: the message is the error text the relay sent, or 'refused' when it sent none, and `createPairing` and `approvePairing` pass it on unchanged.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by `createPairing` with the message 'A newer pairing code replaced this one.' when the status published after opening does not carry this offer while some offer is still open.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by `createPairing` with the message 'The pairing offer could not be opened.' when the status published after opening does not carry this offer and no offer is open.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by `approvePairing`, before anything is approved, with the message 'Only projects opened on this computer can be shared.', when an approved project id is not among the registered projects.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Propagated from the registry's `list()` with the message 'Invalid project registry.'; `approvePairing` awaits it before approving anything, so the approval rejects with it.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown by `approvePairing` with the message 'This pairing request is no longer waiting.' when, after its waits, the open offer has no request from this device under this pairing id, so nothing is approved.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Propagated from the host pairing service's `approve` with the message 'There is no pairing request to approve.' when no live request has this pairing id at that moment, so nothing is approved.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Propagated from the host pairing service's `approve` with the message 'This is not the phone that was shown.' when the device id in the approval is not that of the waiting request, so nothing is approved.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Propagated from the record store through `saved()` with the message 'OS encryption is required for remote access.' when OS encryption is unavailable while the record is written; `approvePairing`, `revokeDevice`, `dropped` and `seen` (for a known device) await it, and file-system errors from the same write are passed on unchanged.

errors.name: RemoteFailure
errors.description: Thrown by `RemoteInputValidator` with code `invalid-message` and the message 'The request was not understood.' when the input of `approvePairing`, `denyPairing` or `revokeDevice` does not have the exact keys and values it must have.
